events.title: Renaissance
events.summary: Revival of classical learning, art and enquiry, beginning in Italy.

events.title: Black Death in Europe
events.summary: Population loss and labour scarcity deepened the feudal crisis; England affected in 1348.

events.title: Ottomans capture Constantinople
events.summary: Increased interest in alternative Asian routes; existing trade did not simply cease.

events.title: Dias's expedition begins
events.summary: Portuguese exploration sought a route around southern Africa.

events.title: Dias rounds the Cape
events.summary: Southern African route opened; Cape of Storms became Cape of Good Hope.

events.title: Columbus reaches the Americas
events.summary: Sailed for Spain; did not reach India.

events.title: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut
events.summary: Cape route to India; Zamorin ruled Calicut, Manuel I ruled Portugal.

events.title: Cabral's expedition
events.summary: Reached Brazil and India; conflict at Calicut strengthened Portuguese links with Cochin.

events.title: Mercantilist policy
events.summary: Bullion, protected commerce and colonial monopoly link State power to trade.

events.title: Merchant capitalism expands
events.summary: Trade, credit and joint-stock enterprise connect distant markets and producers.

events.title: Reformation
events.summary: Challenges to Catholic authority and emergence of Protestant churches.

events.title: Da Gama returns to India
events.summary: Armed Portuguese commerce expands.

events.title: Portuguese fort at Cochin
events.summary: Fortification is distinct from establishing a trading factory.

events.title: Almeida's viceroyalty
events.summary: First viceroy of Estado da Índia; Blue Water naval policy.

events.title: Portuguese fort at Cannanore
events.summary: Part of the coastal network supporting armed trade.

events.title: Battle of Chaul
events.summary: Almeida's son Lourenço killed; distinguish from the following year's Diu victory.

events.title: Albuquerque's governorship
events.summary: Strategic territorial and maritime bases consolidate Portuguese power.

events.title: Battle of Diu
events.summary: Almeida defeated a fleet including Egyptian Mamluk and Gujarat forces.

events.title: Goa captured by Albuquerque
events.summary: Taken from Bijapur Sultanate; not in 1499.

events.title: Portuguese capture Malacca
events.summary: Control of an important Southeast Asian maritime choke point.

events.title: Portuguese take Hormuz
events.summary: Persian Gulf base completes a strategic port network.

events.title: First Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi; comparison in the chapter's PYQ explanation.

events.title: Nuno da Cunha's governorship
events.summary: Associated with Goa headquarters and Diu fortification agreement.

events.title: Portuguese headquarters move to Goa
events.summary: Cochin replaced as the principal administrative centre.

events.title: Diu fortification agreement
events.summary: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat permitted Portuguese fortification under Mughal pressure.

events.title: Printing press at Goa
events.summary: Early printing and missionary/vernacular publishing.

events.title: Battle of Talikota
events.summary: Vijayanagara defeated; its political lineage did not disappear immediately.

events.title: Iberian Union
events.summary: Portuguese Crown linked to Spain; wider European conflicts affected overseas power.

events.title: Houtman reaches Banten, Java
events.summary: Dutch maritime expansion; this voyage did not reach India.

events.title: English merchants organise
events.summary: Enterprise preceded the East India Company charter.

events.title: English East India Company charter
events.summary: Elizabeth I granted the company a trading monopoly. Elizabeth I’s royal charter, not an Act of Parliament.

events.title: Pre-territorial Company commerce
events.summary: Bullion and goods financed Indian manufactures; political control later changed procurement.

events.title: Dutch VOC founded
events.summary: United company with chartered commercial and quasi-State powers.

events.title: Dutch factory at Masulipatnam
events.summary: Earliest Dutch factory in India; Pulicat is earliest only among certain PYQ choices.

events.title: Dutch factory at Petapuli
events.summary: Petapuli/Nizampatnam joins the Coromandel trading network.

events.title: Guru Arjan executed
events.summary: Important turning point in Sikh–Mughal relations.

events.title: Hawkins arrives at Surat
events.summary: Came on Hector; later travelled to Jahangir's court.

events.title: Hawkins at Jahangir's court
events.summary: Commercial negotiations obstructed by Portuguese opposition.

events.title: Dutch base at Pulicat
events.summary: Major headquarters, Fort Geldria and pagoda coinage.

events.title: English factory at Masulipatnam
events.summary: First English factory in South India.

events.title: Battle of Swally/Suvali
events.summary: Thomas Best defeated Portuguese naval forces near Surat.

events.title: English factory permitted at Surat
events.summary: Permission under Jahangir after Swally.

events.title: Thomas Roe's embassy
events.summary: James I's ambassador negotiated at Jahangir's court, not Akbar's.

events.title: Danish East India Company founded
events.summary: Charter date differs from the later Tranquebar settlement.

events.title: Danish settlement at Tranquebar
events.summary: Tharangambadi near Tanjore; Fort Dansborg.

events.title: Amboyna incident
events.summary: Dutch executions of English merchants and others intensified commercial rivalry.

events.title: Company gains judicial powers
events.summary: One stage in the English Company's acquisition of governmental functions.

events.title: Golconda Golden Farman
events.summary: Trading concessions associated with an annual payment of 500 pagodas.

events.title: English factories in Odisha
events.summary: Hariharpur and Balasore: first English footholds in Eastern India.

events.title: Madras acquired for Company settlement
events.summary: Day and Cogan obtained land from Damarla Venkatadri Nayak under the Vijayanagara lineage.

events.title: Fort St George built
events.summary: First English fort in India; distinguish from Fort William in Calcutta.

events.title: English factory at Hugli
events.summary: Shah Shuja's permission; Bengal trade network expands.

events.title: Anglo-Portuguese marriage treaty
events.summary: Bombay promised in the Catherine–Charles II marriage arrangement.

events.title: Company authorised armed shipping
events.summary: Further development of military capacity under charter.

events.title: Catherine of Braganza marries Charles II
events.summary: Wedding date differs from 1661 treaty and 1668 Company transfer.

events.title: Dutch take Cochin from Portuguese
events.summary: Fort Kochi later passed to British control; distinguish the princely Cochin kingdom.

events.title: French East India Company founded
events.summary: Colbert's initiative under Louis XIV.

events.title: French expedition to Surat
events.summary: Preceded the factory established in 1668.

events.title: Bombay transferred to English Company
events.summary: Crown lease at £10 annual rent; later western administrative base.

events.title: French factory at Surat
events.summary: First major French Indian commercial foothold in this sequence.

events.title: French factory at Masulipatnam
events.summary: French trade expands along the Coromandel Coast.

events.title: Bellanger arrives at Pondicherry
events.summary: Precedes François Martin's development of the settlement.

events.title: François Martin develops Pondicherry
events.summary: Local grant from Sher Khan Lodi, Bijapur's representative.

events.title: Guru Tegh Bahadur executed at Delhi
events.summary: Gobind Singh succeeded as Guru aged nine.

events.title: Company gains further war/peace powers
events.summary: Charter strengthens quasi-State military functions.

events.title: Child's War against Aurangzeb
events.summary: Company defeated; trade resumed after submission and fine.

events.title: Sambhaji executed; Shahu captured
events.summary: Rajaram and later Tarabai sustained Maratha resistance.

events.title: Chandernagore consolidated
events.summary: French Bengal trading base develops in the late seventeenth century.

events.title: Company purchases Fort St David
events.summary: Southern base near Cuddalore.

events.title: Dutch headquarters shift to Nagapattinam
events.summary: Replaced Pulicat as principal Dutch Coromandel headquarters.

events.title: Job Charnock settles at Sutanuti
events.summary: Company foothold; does not imply Calcutta had no earlier inhabitants.

events.title: Bengal trading concession
events.summary: Company privilege against ₹3,000 annual payment.

events.title: Dutch seize Pondicherry
events.summary: French possession temporarily interrupted.

events.title: Calcutta fortification begins
events.summary: Fort William developed around 1700; do not collapse the stages.

events.title: Treaty of Ryswick
events.summary: Provided for French restoration at Pondicherry; actual return followed in 1699.

events.title: Company acquires three-village zamindari
events.summary: Sutanuti, Kalikata and Gobindapur, with Azim-us-Shan's permission.

events.title: Khalsa founded
events.summary: Guru Gobind Singh; lasting community and martial institutions.

events.title: Pondicherry returned to French
events.summary: Distinguish actual restoration from the 1697 treaty.

events.title: Sawai Jai Singh II's reign
events.summary: Jaipur, observatories and scientific patronage.

events.title: Fort William and Bengal presidency develop
events.summary: Company's Bengal settlements become an administrative centre.

events.title: Murshid Quli Khan becomes Bengal diwan
events.summary: Revenue authority precedes combined governorship in 1717.

events.title: Rajaram dies; Tarabai's regency
events.summary: Maratha resistance continued through Shivaji II's regency.

events.title: Aurangzeb dies
events.summary: Succession struggle; regional autonomy accelerates without an immediate end to the dynasty.

events.title: Bahadur Shah I's reign
events.summary: Muazzam/Shah Alam I; conciliatory measures alongside Sikh conflict.

events.title: Shahu released
events.summary: Return sharpened conflict with Tarabai; release associated with Azam Shah/Zulfiqar Khan.

events.title: Battle of Jajau
events.summary: Bahadur Shah defeated Azam in the Mughal succession struggle.

events.title: Banda Singh Bahadur's resistance
events.summary: Agrarian mobilisation and armed challenge continued despite repression.

events.title: Guru Gobind Singh dies
events.summary: Sikh community institutions and armed mobilisation continued.

events.title: Rajput alliances renew autonomy
events.summary: Marwar, Amber and Mewar cooperate amid weakening imperial control.

events.title: Kam Bakhsh defeated near Hyderabad
events.summary: Bahadur Shah secured victory over another succession rival.

events.title: Saadatullah Khan in Carnatic
events.summary: Arcot-based Nawab nominated Dost Ali as successor.

events.title: Daud Khan Panni–Shahu arrangement
events.summary: Chauth/sardeshmukhi arrangement later confirmed under Jahandar Shah.

events.title: Jahandar Shah's reign
events.summary: Zulfiqar Khan's support secured the throne; Farrukhsiyar defeated him.

events.title: Asaf Jah becomes Deccan governor
events.summary: Precedes his wazirship and foundation of autonomous Hyderabad.

events.title: Balaji Vishwanath as Peshwa
events.summary: Diplomacy and the 1719 sanad strengthen Maratha claims.

events.title: Farrukhsiyar's reign
events.summary: Sayyid-supported emperor; commercial farman and court conflict.

events.title: Sayyid brothers' ascendancy
events.summary: Abdullah Khan as wazir; Husain Ali as Mir Bakshi.

events.title: Farrukhabad founded
events.summary: Muhammad Khan Bangash; named after Farrukhsiyar.

events.title: Banda Bahadur captured
events.summary: Gurdas Nangal, near Gurdaspur.

events.title: Banda Bahadur executed at Delhi
events.summary: Sikh resistance survived repression.

events.title: Farrukhsiyar's Company farman
events.summary: Bengal concessions against ₹3,000 annually; dastak misuse later creates conflict.

events.title: Murshid Quli combines Bengal offices
events.summary: Nazim and diwan authority together; Murshidabad-based autonomy.

events.title: Farrukhsiyar deposed and killed
events.summary: Sayyid coalition, assisted by Balaji Vishwanath, removes the emperor.

events.title: Mughal sanad recognises Maratha claims
events.summary: Chauth/sardeshmukhi in six Deccan subahs; linked service and tribute obligations.

events.title: Muhammad Shah's reign
events.summary: Roshan Akhtar/Rangeela; regional breakup and Nadir's invasion.

events.title: Rafi-ud-Darajat and Shah Jahan II
events.summary: Two short-lived Sayyid nominees; distinguish Shah Jahan II from III.

events.title: Baji Rao I as Peshwa
events.summary: Northern expansion and rapid cavalry campaigns.

events.title: Sayyid ascendancy broken
events.summary: Rival nobles including Nizam-ul-Mulk undermined their power.

events.title: Asaf Jah serves as Mughal wazir
events.summary: Returns to Deccan and consolidates independent authority.

events.title: Saadat Khan establishes Awadh
events.summary: Burhan-ul-Mulk's provincial authority becomes hereditary.

events.title: Saadat Khan reorganises Awadh revenue
events.summary: Paid forces and stronger provincial finance support autonomy.

events.title: Battle of Shakar Kheda
events.summary: Asaf Jah defeated Mubariz Khan; autonomous Hyderabad consolidated.

events.title: Jaipur founded
events.summary: Sawai Jai Singh II's planned capital and scientific/cultural patronage.

events.title: Shuja-ud-Din in Bengal
events.summary: Murshid Quli's son-in-law succeeds him.

events.title: Marthanda Varma in Travancore
events.summary: Territorial consolidation and a reorganised army.

events.title: Dost Ali in Carnatic
events.summary: Maratha attack ended his rule in 1740.

events.title: Maratha campaigning against Sidis
events.summary: One strand of Baji Rao-era western expansion.

events.title: Baji Rao I raids Delhi
events.summary: Exposes imperial military vulnerability.

events.title: Nadir Shah's invasion
events.summary: Persian intervention culminates in Karnal and Delhi plunder.

events.title: Battle of Karnal and sack of Delhi
events.summary: Muhammad Shah defeated; massacre/plunder and removal of Peacock Throne/Koh-i-Noor.

events.title: Chimaji Appa captures Bassein
events.summary: Maratha victory against Portuguese; distinguish from the 1802 Bassein treaty.

events.title: Safdar Jung in Awadh
events.summary: Became imperial wazir in 1748; Nawab-Wazir connection.

events.title: Sarfaraz Khan in Bengal
events.summary: Shuja-ud-Din's son defeated by Alivardi at Giria.

events.title: Alivardi Khan in Bengal
events.summary: Bargi raids, provincial finance and restrictions on European fortification.

events.title: Balaji Baji Rao as Peshwa
events.summary: Nana Saheb; expansion to zenith followed by Panipat setback.

events.title: Battle of Giria
events.summary: Alivardi defeated/killed Sarfaraz and took Bengal.

events.title: Maratha/Bargi raids in Bengal
events.summary: Repeated raids culminate in the 1751 settlement.

events.title: Marathas attack Carnatic
events.summary: Dost Ali killed; Chanda Sahib captured and taken to Satara.

events.title: War of Austrian Succession
events.summary: European conflict provides immediate context for First Carnatic War.

events.title: Battle of Colachel
events.summary: Marthanda Varma's Travancore forces defeated Dutch.

events.title: Dupleix governs French India
events.summary: Succession intervention and territorial concessions extend French influence.

events.title: Zakariya Khan dies
events.summary: Punjab provincial succession conflict opens further space for Sikh mobilisation.

events.title: Battle of Adyar/St Thomé
events.summary: Paradis's smaller French force defeated Mahfuz Khan's Carnatic army.

events.title: First Carnatic War
events.summary: Austrian Succession conflict extends to India; settlement restores Madras.

events.title: French capture Madras
events.summary: La Bourdonnais's fleet supports French operations under Dupleix.

events.title: Nadir Shah assassinated; Durrani power founded
events.summary: Ahmad Shah Abdali founded Afghan power, not a successor Persian dynasty.

events.title: Abdali's first invasion repulsed
events.summary: Beginning of the chapter's 1748–67 invasion sequence.

events.title: Ahmad Shah Bahadur's reign
events.summary: Weak court and kingmakers; Punjab/Multan ceded in 1752.

events.title: Asaf Jah I dies
events.summary: Nasir Jung–Muzaffar Jung succession dispute creates French/English opportunities.

events.title: Chanda Sahib released
events.summary: Resumes Carnatic claim with French-backed Muzaffar Jung.

events.title: Safdar Jung becomes imperial wazir
events.summary: Combines Awadh rulership with a central imperial office.

events.title: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
events.summary: Madras to English; Louisbourg to French; First Carnatic War ends.

events.title: Abdali pressures Punjab
events.summary: Conflict over Muin-ul-Mulk and frontier authority continues.

events.title: Second Carnatic War
events.summary: Linked succession disputes in Hyderabad and Carnatic.

events.title: Shahu dies
events.summary: Succession and Sangola arrangement further consolidate Peshwa power.

events.title: Battle of Ambur
events.summary: Anwaruddin killed; Chanda Sahib installed, Muhammad Ali retreats to Trichinopoly.

events.title: Nasir Jung killed; Muzaffar Jung installed
events.summary: French-backed Hyderabad succession; grants strengthen Dupleix.

events.title: Sangola arrangement
events.summary: Rajaram II/Ramraja and Peshwa authority; do not confuse with Shivaji's son Rajaram.

events.title: Bengal–Maratha settlement
events.summary: Orissa passes to Maratha control; Bengal/Bihar annual chauth ₹12 lakh.

events.title: Siege of Arcot
events.summary: Clive defends the captured Carnatic capital through the subsequent siege.

events.title: Muzaffar Jung killed; Salabat Jung installed
events.summary: Bussy maintains French influence at Hyderabad.

events.title: Clive captures Arcot
events.summary: Diversion relieves pressure on Muhammad Ali at Trichinopoly.

events.title: Kaveripak and relief of Trichinopoly
events.summary: English successes; Lawrence relieves Trichinopoly, Chanda Sahib killed in Tanjore hands.

events.title: Punjab and Multan ceded to Abdali
events.summary: Afghan influence grows during Ahmad Shah Bahadur's reign.

events.title: Bussy obtains four Northern Circars
events.summary: Mustafanagar, Ellore, Rajahmundry, Chicacole support French finances.

events.title: Gomastha procurement in the supplied account
events.summary: Company paid agents replaced intermediaries; coercive power expanded after Plassey.

events.title: Ahmad Shah Bahadur deposed/blinded
events.summary: Imad-ul-Mulk's kingmaking raises Alamgir II.

events.title: Alamgir II's reign
events.summary: Abdali's Delhi sack and Plassey occur during his rule; murdered in 1759.

events.title: Dupleix recalled; Godeheu succeeds
events.summary: French commercial/financial concerns reverse his intervention policy.

events.title: Pondicherry agreement
events.summary: Godeheu–Saunders agreement ending Second Carnatic War; not 1755.

events.title: Shuja-ud-Daulah in Awadh
events.summary: Panipat ally of Abdali; later coalition at Buxar and Allahabad settlement.

events.title: Danish settlement at Serampore
events.summary: Frederiksnagore in Bengal; education and missionary printing later important.

events.title: French-assisted arsenal at Dindigul
events.summary: Hyder's military modernisation includes arms manufacture.

events.title: Abdali's Delhi expedition
events.summary: Delhi plundered; Afghan appointments and Timur's position established.

events.title: Seven Years' War
events.summary: European/global context for Third Carnatic War, often dated 1757–63 in Indian timelines.

events.title: Siraj-ud-Daulah in Bengal
events.summary: Court factionalism and Company trade/fortification disputes culminate at Plassey.

events.title: Suraj Mal's Bharatpur ascendancy
events.summary: Jat State-building, diplomacy and regional power; survives his death.

events.title: Third Carnatic War
events.summary: Lally's campaign, Wandiwash, fall of Pondicherry and Paris settlement.

events.title: Fort William falls to Siraj
events.summary: Calcutta renamed Alinagar; Holwell's Black Hole account has disputed numbers/responsibility.

events.title: Company obtains zamindari of 24 Parganas
events.summary: Revenue rights expanded after Plassey, preceding Diwani.

events.title: Mercantilist phase of colonial economy
events.summary: Interpretive phase: monopoly, tribute and revenue-financed export purchases.

events.title: Mir Jafar's first Nawabship
events.summary: 24-Parganas, payments and dependence; Dutch intervention fails.

events.title: Company recovers Calcutta
events.summary: Clive's land expedition and Admiral Watson's naval support.

events.title: Treaty of Alinagar
events.summary: Commercial privileges, fortification permission and compensation restored.

events.title: Company captures Chandernagore
events.summary: French Bengal base weakened before Plassey.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: Clive defeated Siraj amid Mir Jafar/Rai Durlabh's non-cooperation; Company becomes kingmaker. Indian revenue and political power increasingly financed trade purchases.

events.title: Clive's first Bengal governorship
events.summary: Conventional governorship dates; political ascendancy began with Plassey in 1757.

events.title: Dharma Raja in Travancore
events.summary: Rama Varma; scholarship, arts and resistance to external pressure.

events.title: Marathas expel Timur and occupy Punjab
events.summary: Raghunath Rao displaces Afghan influence; immediate context for Abdali's later return.

events.title: Lally arrives in India
events.summary: Captures Fort St David but fails to secure lasting strategic advantage.

events.title: Abdali's Panipat campaign
events.summary: Countered Maratha occupation of Punjab and culminated in Panipat.

events.title: Alamgir II murdered
events.summary: Imad-ul-Mulk's court violence precedes competing imperial claims.

events.title: Shah Alam II's reign
events.summary: Early exile, Buxar, Maratha return to Delhi and later Company protection.

events.title: Shah Jahan III's brief claim
events.summary: Muhi-ul-Millat's claim overlaps Shah Alam II's; not a neat exclusive succession.

events.title: Battle of Bedara/Biderra
events.summary: Company defeats Dutch Bengal intervention; does not instantly end every Dutch settlement.

events.title: British Industrial Revolution
events.summary: Mechanised textile/iron production and steam alter colonial trading interests. Machine-made competition and British demand changed Indian trade.

events.title: Vansittart succeeds Clive
events.summary: Bengal administration replaces Mir Jafar with Mir Qasim.

events.title: Battle of Wandiwash
events.summary: Eyre Coote defeated Lally; Bussy captured; decisive English–French turning point.

events.title: Mir Qasim becomes Nawab
events.summary: Cedes Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong; reorganises revenue and army, shifts capital to Munger. Company acquired Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong revenue rights.

events.title: Hyder Ali takes effective power in Mysore
events.summary: Wadiyar monarchy initially retained; military and territorial consolidation follows.

events.title: Madhav Rao I as Peshwa
events.summary: Maratha Resurrection; strengthened regional/northern influence.

events.title: Third Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Abdali defeats Bhau/Vishwas Rao's Marathas; severe setback followed by later recovery.

events.title: Pondicherry surrenders
events.summary: British siege ends Lally's resistance; French commercial settlements later restored.

events.title: Balaji Baji Rao dies
events.summary: After Panipat; Madhav Rao I begins the period of Maratha recovery.

events.title: British occupation of Manila
events.summary: Brief occupation; not permanent annexation of the Philippines.

events.title: Vansittart–Mir Qasim compromise
events.summary: 9% duty proposal on private inland trade; rejected by Calcutta Council.

events.title: Mir Jafar restored
events.summary: Restoration precedes Buxar; Najm-ud-Daulah succeeds in 1765.

events.title: Mir Qasim abolishes inland duties
events.summary: Indian merchants gain parity; Ellis's Patna attack precipitates war.

events.title: Mir Qasim defeated and flees to Awadh
events.summary: Coalition with Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II develops.

events.title: Suraj Mal dies fighting Rohillas
events.summary: Bharatpur kingdom continues beyond his death.

events.title: Treaty of Paris
events.summary: Third Carnatic War ends; French settlements restored under restrictions.

events.title: Spinning jenny
events.summary: Hargreaves's invention; distinct from Arkwright's later water frame.

events.title: Battle of Buxar
events.summary: Hector Munro defeats allied Awadh/imperial forces; Mir Qasim part of the wider coalition.

events.title: Clive's second governorship
events.summary: Settlements with Awadh, emperor and Bengal consolidate Company power.

events.title: Dual government in Bengal
events.summary: Company power and revenue control; nominal Nawab/intermediary administration; weak accountability. Company Diwani and nominal Nawabi Nizamat separated power from responsibility.

events.title: Najm-ud-Daulah becomes Bengal Nawab
events.summary: Military/foreign affairs and key appointments fall under Company control.

events.title: Imperial diwani grant
events.summary: Shah Alam II grants Bengal, Bihar and Orissa revenue rights; ₹26 lakh annual imperial payment. Diwani financed export purchases and established Company revenue control.

events.title: Awadh settlement at Allahabad
events.summary: Shuja pays ₹50 lakh; Kora/Allahabad ceded; Awadh restored as a buffer.

events.title: Company–Nizam Northern Circars agreement
events.summary: Coastal rights and promised military aid against Hyder contribute to conflict.

events.title: Hyder's Malabar expansion
events.summary: Did not absorb Travancore.

events.title: Lally executed in France
events.summary: Prosecution follows the French defeat in India.

events.title: First Anglo-Mysore War
events.summary: Hyder breaks the initial opposing coalition and reaches the vicinity of Madras.

events.title: Parliament claims annual Company payment
events.summary: £400,000 annual contribution; comprehensive regulation came later.

events.title: Gorkha conquest of Kathmandu
events.summary: Unification and further expansion brought Nepal toward Company frontiers.

events.title: Mahadji Scindia's ascendancy
events.summary: Northern reconstruction, Delhi influence and European-trained brigades.

events.title: Arkwright's water frame
events.summary: Mechanised water-powered spinning supports factory production.

events.title: Bengal famine
events.summary: Drought/crop failure compounded by extraction and administrative failures. Harvest crisis, exactions and weak relief aggravated Bengal famine; mortality estimates uncertain.

events.title: Company favours raw over woven silk
events.summary: Commercial policy encourages raw silk supply while restricting competing finished fabrics.

events.title: Watt's separate-condenser patent
events.summary: Improves existing steam engines; not the first invention of steam power.

events.title: Treaty of Madras
events.summary: Mutual restitution and assistance against third-party attack; favourable peace for Hyder.

events.title: Company fails to aid Hyder against Marathas
events.summary: Breach of expected assistance deepens Mysore's distrust.

events.title: Shah Alam II returns to Delhi
events.summary: Mahadji-led Maratha support restores emperor; return completed in January 1772.

events.title: Carnatic and Tanjore titles or residual sovereignty removed
events.summary: Distinguish titles/pensions from territorial lapse cases.

events.title: First competitive civil-service examination
events.summary: Held in London; practical barriers limited Indian participation.

events.title: Madras Torture Commission report
events.summary: Documented abuse under revenue administration.

events.title: Rishra jute mill established
events.summary: George Acland's mill near Calcutta; British capital prominent.

events.title: Saharanpur Rules
events.summary: Revenue benchmark reduced to about half net rental assets; implementation varied.

events.title: Eastern railway reaches Raniganj
events.summary: Do not date the full service to 1854.

events.title: Awadh annexed
events.summary: Long dependence ends in direct annexation. Outram report supplied misgovernment pretext; Awadh was not a lapse annexation; Wajid Ali Shah removed.

events.title: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras universities founded
events.summary: Followed the educational framework of Wood's Despatch.

events.title: Mandalay founded as capital
events.summary: Mindon's capital foundation was later than his 1853 accession.

events.title: Revolt; Zafar becomes symbolic sovereign
events.summary: Company retakes Delhi and captures the emperor. Annexation and agrarian grievances contributed; crisis led to Crown transfer. Jang Bahadur’s Nepalese forces assisted the British; Nepal did not remain simply neutral.

events.title: Rural mobilisation in northern India
events.summary: Debt, dispossession and revenue grievances contributed to revolt.

events.title: Allahabad provincial seat after the revolt
events.summary: Important provincial administrative centre and venue of the royal proclamation; not established as India’s capital for one day.

events.title: Finance-capital phase
events.summary: Interpretive phase: investment and remitted returns in railways, plantations and mining.

events.title: Zafar tried and deported to Rangoon
events.summary: Mughal dynasty's political removal distinct from his death in 1862.

events.title: Government of India Act receives assent
events.summary: Crown takes Company government; Secretary of State and fifteen-member Council; Stanley first Secretary.

events.title: Queen Victoria's Proclamation
events.summary: Crown takeover from Company; not the beginning of Mughal decline. 1 November Allahabad; treaties, non-annexation, religion and fair employment promises; no responsible government.

events.title: Bengal Rent Act
events.summary: Limited protection for occupancy tenants; did not abolish Permanent Settlement.

events.title: Punjab Lieutenant-Governorship
events.summary: Crown-era administrative arrangement followed earlier Board administration.

events.title: Indian Penal Code enacted
events.summary: Enactment is distinct from its later operational commencement.

events.title: Indian Penal Code commences
events.summary: Correct commencement date; distinguish the 2005 PYQ wording.

events.title: Bahadur Shah Zafar dies
events.summary: Death in exile after the dynasty's removal.

events.title: Naoroji presents England's Debt to India
events.summary: East India Association address developed the drain argument.

events.title: State railway construction expands
events.summary: Policy shifted after early private guaranteed companies.

events.title: East India Company dissolved
events.summary: Legal corporate existence outlasted its government's abolition in 1858.

events.title: Tata's Central India textile company
events.summary: Jamsetji Tata's industrial enterprise preceded Empress Mills opening.

events.title: Great Famine
events.summary: Revenue pressure, poverty, drought and relief/distribution failures increased mortality.

events.title: North-Western Provinces and Oudh administratively associated
events.summary: Association occurred after Awadh's 1856 annexation.

events.title: Empress Mills opens in Nagpur
events.summary: Tata textile enterprise strengthened Indian modern industry.

events.title: Second Anglo-Afghan War
events.summary: Lytton renewed forward intervention; 1879 agreement did not end all fighting.

events.title: Treaty of Gandamak
events.summary: Yakub Khan accepted British external-policy influence and a resident; later uprising reopened conflict.

events.title: Abdur Rahman becomes Amir
events.summary: British external influence continued without permanent annexation.

events.title: Renewed private railway participation
events.summary: Approximate decade; arrangements differed from the earliest guarantees.

events.title: Third Anglo-Burmese War
events.summary: Dufferin; commercial conflict and Thibaw's foreign connections supplied justification.

events.title: Upper Burma annexed
events.summary: Thibaw removed; formal annexation followed the 1885 war.

events.title: R.C. Dutt presides over Congress
events.summary: Economic critique linked to nationalist politics.

events.title: Dutt's Open Letters to Curzon
events.summary: Criticised famine and land-assessment policy.

events.title: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India published
events.summary: Naoroji consolidated an economic critique developed earlier.

events.title: Dutt's Economic History first volume
events.summary: Historical analysis of colonial economic policy; second volume followed in 1904.

events.title: United Provinces name adopted
events.summary: Later name of the North-Western Provinces and Oudh.

events.title: Dutt's Economic History second volume
events.summary: Continued his account of colonial economic change.

events.title: Jamsetji Tata dies
events.summary: Dorabji Tata and associates carried the steel project forward.

events.title: Railway network reaches roughly 45,000 km
events.summary: Rounded textbook network comparison; expansion served commerce and troop movement as well as wider market integration.

events.title: Swadeshi strengthens indigenous enterprise
events.summary: Indian modern industry predated the movement.

events.title: Naoroji's swaraj demand at Calcutta Congress
events.summary: Economic criticism fed the political demand for self-government.

events.title: TISCO incorporated
events.summary: Jamsetji Tata's vision carried forward by Dorabji and associates.

events.title: TISCO begins pig iron production
events.summary: Preceded first steel production.

events.title: TISCO first steel production
events.summary: Correct date is 1912, not 1913.

events.title: Birla enters jute industry
events.summary: Indian industrial enterprise expanded in a British-dominated sector.

events.title: Burma separated from British India
events.summary: Became a distinct British colony.

events.title: Birla jute expansion
events.summary: Approximate decade; later development extends beyond the chapter's principal period.

events.title: Ashok Leyland founded
events.summary: Post-independence enterprise; not evidence of a pre-1947 colonial company.

events.title: French enclaves transfer de facto to India
events.summary: Distinguish practical transfer from 1962 legal transfer.

events.title: Goa, Daman and Diu brought under India
events.summary: Military action ends Portuguese administration.

events.title: French enclave transfer de jure
events.summary: Legal completion follows de facto transfer of 1954.
